sourceNote: Clause numbers and titles follow ETSI EN 301 549 V3.2.1 (2021-03), the version cited in the Official Journal of the EU. Plain-language summaries are original accessibility.build prose, verified against the published standard on 27 August 2026. WCAG-mapped clause summaries reuse this site's criterion descriptions.

rows.title: Meeting functional performance statements
rows.summary: Explains how the functional performance statements in clause 4.2 are used: they describe outcomes that let people locate, identify, and operate ICT functions regardless of physical, cognitive, or sensory ability, and Annex B maps every requirement to them.

rows.title: Usage without vision
rows.summary: Where ICT has visual modes of operation, at least one mode of operation should not require vision at all.

rows.title: Usage with limited vision
rows.summary: Where ICT has visual modes of operation, it should provide features (such as magnification or contrast adjustment) that let people with limited vision use it.

rows.title: Usage without perception of colour
rows.summary: Where ICT has visual modes of operation, at least one visual mode should not depend on the user perceiving colour.

rows.title: Usage without hearing
rows.summary: Where ICT has auditory modes of operation, at least one mode of operation should not require hearing.

rows.title: Usage with limited hearing
rows.summary: Where ICT has auditory modes of operation, it should provide enhanced audio features (such as clarity enhancement or volume boost) for people with limited hearing.

rows.title: Usage with no or limited vocal capability
rows.summary: Where ICT requires vocal input, at least one mode of operation should not require the user to speak.

rows.title: Usage with limited manipulation or strength
rows.summary: Where ICT requires manual actions, it should offer alternatives that do not need fine manipulation, simultaneous actions, or hand strength.

rows.title: Usage with limited reach
rows.summary: Where ICT products are free-standing or installed, every element needed for operation should be within reach of all users, including wheelchair users.

rows.title: Minimize photosensitive seizure triggers
rows.summary: Where ICT has visual modes of operation, at least one mode should minimise the potential for triggering photosensitive seizures.

rows.title: Usage with limited cognition, language or learning
rows.summary: ICT should provide features and presentation that make it simpler to understand, operate, and use for people with limited cognition, language, or learning.

rows.title: Privacy
rows.summary: Where ICT provides accessibility features, using them should not cost the user more privacy than other users get.

rows.title: Closed functionality
rows.summary: ICT with closed functionality must meet the applicable requirements of clauses 5.2 to 13 for those closed functions.

rows.title: Assistive technology
rows.summary: Closed functionality must be operable without the user attaching, connecting, or installing assistive technology, and must meet clauses 5.1.3 to 5.1.6 instead of assuming AT support.

rows.title: Audio output of visual information
rows.summary: Where visual information is needed to use functions closed to screen readers, provide at least one non-visual mode of access (such as speech output) conveying the same information.

rows.title: Auditory output delivery including speech
rows.summary: Auditory output used as non-visual access must be delivered either by a mechanism included with the ICT or through a standard personal headset connection that can be used without vision.

rows.title: Auditory output correlation
rows.summary: Advisory: where information is displayed on screen, auditory output should let the user correlate what they hear with what is on the screen.

rows.title: Speech output user control
rows.summary: Speech output must be interruptible and repeatable on request, where security requirements permit.

rows.title: Speech output automatic interruption
rows.summary: The ICT must interrupt current speech output when a user action occurs and when new speech output begins.

rows.title: Speech output for non-text content
rows.summary: Alternatives for non-text content must be spoken aloud, unless the content is pure decoration or only visual formatting.

rows.title: Speech output for video information
rows.summary: Where pre-recorded video is needed to use closed functions, speech output must present equivalent information for the video content.

rows.title: Masked entry
rows.summary: Speech output must not read masked characters (such as PIN digits) aloud unless the user explicitly chooses audible unmasked entry.

rows.title: Private access to personal data
rows.summary: Auditory output containing private data must only be delivered through a private listening mechanism (such as a headset) or another user-chosen private means.

rows.title: Non-interfering audio output
rows.summary: The ICT must not automatically play interfering audio lasting longer than three seconds at the same time as the speech output.

rows.title: Private listening volume
rows.summary: Where auditory output is delivered through a private listening mechanism, at least one non-visual way to control the volume must exist.

rows.title: Speaker volume
rows.summary: Where auditory output is delivered through speakers, a non-visual incremental volume control with amplification up to at least 65 dBA must be provided.

rows.title: Volume reset
rows.summary: On shared-use ICT, a function must reset the volume to 65 dBA or less after every use.

rows.title: Spoken languages
rows.summary: Speech output must be in the same human language as the displayed content, with narrow exceptions such as proper names, technical terms, and languages the ICT cannot speak.

rows.title: Non-visual error identification
rows.summary: Where an input error is automatically detected, speech output must identify and describe the item in error.

rows.title: Receipts, tickets, and transactional outputs
rows.summary: Receipts, tickets, and other transaction outputs from self-service ICT must have their essential information available via speech output (printed copies themselves are exempt).

rows.title: Functionality closed to text enlargement
rows.summary: Where functionality is closed to text-enlargement features, the ICT must itself provide a mode where text needed for all functionality is legible at distance-appropriate sizes.

rows.title: Visual output for auditory information
rows.summary: Where auditory information is needed to use closed functions, the ICT must provide equivalent visual information, such as captions.

rows.title: Closed functionality
rows.summary: Where functionality is closed to keyboards and keyboard interfaces, all of it must be operable without vision as required by clause 5.1.3.

rows.title: Input focus
rows.summary: Where input focus can be moved to an element, it must also be movable away from that element using the same mechanism, so focus cannot get trapped.

rows.title: Access without speech
rows.summary: Where speech is needed to operate closed functions, at least one alternative input mechanism that does not require speech must be provided.

rows.title: Activation of accessibility features
rows.summary: Documented accessibility features must be activatable without relying on a method that the feature's target users cannot use.

rows.title: Biometrics
rows.summary: ICT using biometrics must not make one particular biological characteristic the only way to identify a user or control the ICT.

rows.title: Preservation of accessibility information during conversion
rows.summary: When ICT converts information, it must preserve all documented non-proprietary accessibility information the destination format can hold.

rows.title: Means of operation
rows.summary: Operable parts requiring grasping, pinching, or wrist-twisting must have an accessible alternative means of operation.

rows.title: Operable parts discernibility
rows.summary: Every operable part must be discernible without vision and without performing its action, for example through tactile marking.

rows.title: Tactile or auditory status
rows.summary: Where a locking or toggle control shows its status visually, at least one mode must expose the status by touch or sound as well.

rows.title: Visual status
rows.summary: Where a locking or toggle control exposes its status non-visually, at least one mode must make the status visually determinable too.

rows.title: Key repeat
rows.summary: A key-repeat function that cannot be turned off must allow a repeat delay of at least 2 seconds and a rate adjustable down to 1 character per 2 seconds.

rows.title: Double-strike key acceptance
rows.summary: On keyboards and keypads, the delay for rejecting an accidental identical second keystroke must be adjustable up to at least 0.5 seconds.

rows.title: Simultaneous user actions
rows.summary: Any operation requiring simultaneous user actions must have at least one mode of operation that does not.

rows.title: Audio bandwidth for speech
rows.summary: Two-way voice communication must support speech encoding with an upper frequency limit of at least 7 000 Hz, for intelligible audio quality.

rows.title: RTT communication
rows.summary: ICT providing two-way voice communication must also provide two-way real-time text (RTT), except where that would require adding input or output hardware.

rows.title: Concurrent voice and text
rows.summary: Where voice and RTT are both provided, the ICT must allow concurrent voice and text over a single connection.

rows.title: Visually distinguishable display
rows.summary: Displayed sent RTT text must be visually distinguishable from and separated from received text.

rows.title: Programmatically determinable send and receive direction
rows.summary: The send and receive direction of RTT text must be programmatically determinable, unless the RTT is closed functionality, so screen readers can voice who typed what.

rows.title: Speaker identification
rows.summary: Where speaker identification is available for voice, it must also be available for RTT participants.

rows.title: Visual indicator of Audio with RTT
rows.summary: Where voice and RTT are both active, a real-time visual indicator of audio activity must be shown on the display.

rows.title: Interoperability
rows.summary: ICT with RTT functionality must interoperate with other RTT ICT using the applicable standard mechanisms listed in the clause (such as ITU-T T.140 for IP telephony).

rows.title: RTT responsiveness
rows.summary: RTT input must reach the network or platform within 500 ms of the smallest reliably composed unit of text being available, so text truly flows in real time.

rows.title: Caller ID
rows.summary: Caller ID and similar functions must be available in text form and be programmatically determinable, unless the functionality is closed.

rows.title: Alternatives to voice-based services
rows.summary: Where real-time voice services offer voicemail, auto-attendant, or interactive voice response, the same information and tasks must be achievable without hearing or speech.

rows.title: Resolution
rows.summary: Real-time video used with voice communication must support at least QVGA resolution, and preferably VGA or better.

rows.title: Frame rate
rows.summary: Real-time video used with voice communication must support at least 20 frames per second, and preferably 30 or more.

rows.title: Synchronization between audio and video
rows.summary: The time difference between speech and video presented to the user must not exceed 100 ms, keeping lip-reading viable.

rows.title: Visual indicator of audio with video
rows.summary: Where video is part of two-way voice communication, a real-time visual indicator of audio activity must be provided.

rows.title: Speaker identification with video (sign language) communication
rows.summary: Where speaker identification exists for voice users, an equivalent means must identify who is currently signing in real-time video.

rows.title: Alternatives to video-based services
rows.summary: Advisory: where real-time video services offer answering machine, auto-attendant, or interactive response facilities, users should be able to access them through video as well.

rows.title: Captioning playback
rows.summary: ICT that displays video with synchronized audio must have a mode that displays available captions, including user-selectable closed captions.

rows.title: Captioning synchronization
rows.summary: Caption display must stay synchronized: within 100 ms of the caption timestamp for recorded material, and within 100 ms of caption availability for live captions.

rows.title: Preservation of captioning
rows.summary: ICT that transmits, converts, or records video must preserve caption data so captions can still be displayed correctly downstream.

rows.title: Captions characteristics
rows.summary: Users must be able to adapt caption display characteristics (such as size, colour, and background) except where captions are unmodifiable characters.

rows.title: Spoken subtitles
rows.summary: ICT displaying video with synchronized audio must offer spoken output of the available captions (spoken subtitles), where caption content is programmatically determinable.

rows.title: Audio description playback
rows.summary: A mechanism must exist to select and play available audio description to the default audio channel.

rows.title: Audio description synchronization
rows.summary: Audio description playback must stay synchronized with the audio-visual content.

rows.title: Preservation of audio description
rows.summary: ICT that transmits, converts, or records video must preserve audio description data for downstream playback.

rows.title: User controls for captions and audio description
rows.summary: Controls to activate captions and audio description must sit at the same level of interaction as the primary media controls, not buried in deeper menus.

rows.title: Generic requirements
rows.summary: The generic requirements of clause 5 also apply to hardware.

rows.title: Standard connections
rows.summary: Where hardware provides input or output connection points, at least one must use an industry-standard non-proprietary format, directly or via commercially available adapters.

rows.title: Colour
rows.summary: Hardware must not use colour as the only visual means of conveying information, indicating an action, prompting a response, or distinguishing an element.

rows.title: Speech volume range
rows.summary: Hardware with speech output must allow speech volume adjustment over a range of at least 18 dB.

rows.title: Incremental volume control
rows.summary: Where the volume control is incremental, at least one intermediate step of 12 dB gain above the lowest setting must exist.

rows.title: Fixed-line devices
rows.summary: Fixed-line handsets held to the ear must provide magnetic coupling meeting ETSI ES 200 381-1, marked with the T symbol, for hearing-aid users.

rows.title: Wireless communication devices
rows.summary: Wireless communication devices held to the ear must provide magnetic coupling to hearing technologies meeting ETSI ES 200 381-2.

rows.title: Forward or side reach
rows.summary: Stationary ICT must meet either the forward-reach dimensions of clause 8.3.2 or the side-reach dimensions of clause 8.3.3.

rows.title: Unobstructed high forward reach
rows.summary: With unobstructed forward reach, at least one of each type of operable part must be no higher than 1 220 mm above the floor.

rows.title: Unobstructed low forward reach
rows.summary: With unobstructed forward reach, at least one of each type of operable part must be no lower than 380 mm above the floor.

rows.title: Clear space
rows.summary: Where an integral obstruction hinders access, clear space must extend beneath it at least as far as the obstruction's own depth.

rows.title: Obstructed (< 510 mm) forward reach
rows.summary: With an integral obstruction shallower than 510 mm, forward reach to at least one of each type of operable part must be no higher than 1 220 mm.

rows.title: Obstructed (< 635 mm) forward reach
rows.summary: With an integral obstruction between 510 mm and 635 mm deep, forward reach must be no higher than 1 120 mm.

rows.title: Knee and toe clearance width
rows.summary: Knee and toe clearance under an integral obstacle that forms part of the access space must be at least 760 mm wide.

rows.title: Toe clearance
rows.summary: Toe clearance (space under 230 mm above the floor) must extend no more than 635 mm under the whole obstacle and meet the clause's minimum depth and height dimensions.

rows.title: Knee clearance
rows.summary: Knee clearance (230 mm to 685 mm above the floor) must meet the clause's depth and height dimensions so a seated user can approach.

rows.title: Unobstructed high side reach
rows.summary: With unobstructed side reach (obstruction under 255 mm), at least one of each type of operable part must be within a high side reach of no more than 1 220 mm.

rows.title: Unobstructed low side reach
rows.summary: With unobstructed side reach, at least one of each type of operable part must be no lower than a side reach of 380 mm.

rows.title: Obstructed (≤ 255 mm) side reach
rows.summary: With an integral side obstruction up to 255 mm deep and under 865 mm high, the side reach must be no higher than 1 220 mm.

rows.title: Obstructed (≤ 610 mm) side reach
rows.summary: With an integral side obstruction between 255 mm and 610 mm deep and under 865 mm high, the side reach must be no higher than 1 170 mm.

rows.title: Change in level
rows.summary: Any change of floor level within or entering stationary ICT must be ramped at no steeper than 1:48, with small level changes excepted.

rows.title: Clear floor or ground space
rows.summary: An operating area within stationary ICT must provide clear floor space of at least 760 mm by 1 220 mm.

rows.title: Forward approach
rows.summary: Where a forward approach into an alcove deeper than 610 mm is necessary, the access space must be at least 915 mm wide.

rows.title: Parallel approach
rows.summary: Where a parallel approach to an alcove deeper than 380 mm is possible, the access space must be at least 1 525 mm wide.

rows.title: Visibility
rows.summary: At least one of each type of display screen must be legible from a point 1 015 mm above the centre of the clear floor space.

rows.title: Installation instructions
rows.summary: Installation instructions must be available and must cover installing the ICT so its operable parts and displays stay within accessible reach and sight ranges.

rows.title: Numeric keys
rows.summary: Physical numeric keypads laid out in a rectangle must have a tactilely distinct number five key.

rows.title: Means of operation of mechanical parts
rows.summary: Mechanical controls requiring grasping, pinching, or wrist-twisting must have an accessible alternative means of operation.

rows.title: Force of operation of mechanical parts
rows.summary: Mechanical controls requiring more than 22.2 N of force must have an alternative requiring less than 22.2 N.

rows.title: Keys, tickets and fare cards
rows.summary: Keys, tickets, and fare cards whose orientation matters for further use must have tactilely discernible orientation.

rows.title: Tactile indication of speech mode
rows.summary: Shared-use ICT with speech output must give a tactile indication (such as braille) of how to start the speech mode.

rows.title: Non-text content
rows.summary: All non-text content has appropriate text alternatives that serve the equivalent purpose.

rows.title: Audio-only and video-only (pre-recorded)
rows.summary: Provide alternatives for prerecorded audio-only and video-only content.

rows.title: Captions (pre-recorded)
rows.summary: Captions are provided for all prerecorded audio content in synchronized media.

rows.title: Audio description or media alternative (pre-recorded)
rows.summary: Audio description or full text alternative is provided for prerecorded video content.

rows.title: Captions (live)
rows.summary: Captions are provided for all live audio content in synchronized media.

rows.title: Audio description (pre-recorded)
rows.summary: Audio description is provided for all prerecorded video content.

rows.title: Info and relationships
rows.summary: Information, structure, and relationships can be programmatically determined.

rows.title: Meaningful sequence
rows.summary: Content can be presented in a meaningful sequence without losing meaning.

rows.title: Sensory characteristics
rows.summary: Instructions don't rely solely on sensory characteristics of components.

rows.title: Orientation
rows.summary: Content does not restrict its view to a single display orientation.

rows.title: Identify input purpose
rows.summary: The purpose of input fields can be programmatically determined.

rows.title: Use of colour
rows.summary: Color is not used as the only visual means of conveying information.

rows.title: Audio control
rows.summary: Audio that plays automatically can be paused, stopped, or controlled.

rows.title: Contrast (minimum)
rows.summary: Text has a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 (3:1 for large text).

rows.title: Resize text
rows.summary: Text can be resized up to 200% without loss of content or functionality.

rows.title: Images of text
rows.summary: Text is used instead of images of text, except for customizable or essential images.

rows.title: Void
rows.summary: Void. This slot keeps WCAG numbering alignment; the corresponding WCAG 2.1 criterion is Level AAA and is not required by EN 301 549.

rows.title: Void
rows.summary: Void. This slot keeps WCAG numbering alignment; the corresponding WCAG 2.1 criterion is Level AAA and is not required by EN 301 549.

rows.summary: Void. This slot keeps WCAG numbering alignment; the corresponding WCAG 2.1 criterion is Level AAA and is not required by EN 301 549.

rows.title: Void
rows.summary: Void. This slot keeps WCAG numbering alignment; the corresponding WCAG 2.1 criterion is Level AAA and is not required by EN 301 549.

rows.title: Reflow
rows.summary: Content can be presented without horizontal scrolling at 320 CSS pixels width.

rows.title: Non-text contrast
rows.summary: UI components and graphical objects have sufficient contrast (3:1 minimum).

rows.title: Text spacing
rows.summary: No loss of content when text spacing is adjusted within certain parameters.

rows.title: Content on hover or focus
rows.summary: Additional content triggered by hover or focus can be dismissed and doesn't interfere.

rows.title: Keyboard
rows.summary: All functionality is available from a keyboard interface.

rows.title: No keyboard trap
rows.summary: Focus can be moved away from any component using standard keyboard methods.

rows.title: Void
rows.summary: Void. This slot keeps WCAG numbering alignment; the corresponding WCAG 2.1 criterion is Level AAA and is not required by EN 301 549.

rows.title: Character key shortcuts
rows.summary: Single character key shortcuts can be turned off or remapped.

rows.title: Timing adjustable
rows.summary: Users can turn off, adjust, or extend time limits.

rows.title: Pause, stop, hide
rows.summary: Moving, blinking, or auto-updating content can be paused, stopped, or hidden.

rows.title: Three flashes or below threshold
rows.summary: Content does not contain anything that flashes more than three times per second.

rows.title: Bypass blocks
rows.summary: A mechanism is available to bypass blocks of content that are repeated.

rows.title: Page titled
rows.summary: Web pages have titles that describe topic or purpose.

rows.title: Focus Order
rows.summary: Focusable components receive focus in an order that preserves meaning.

rows.title: Link purpose (in context)
rows.summary: The purpose of each link can be determined from link text or context.

rows.title: Multiple ways
rows.summary: More than one way is available to locate a page within a set of pages.

rows.title: Headings and labels
rows.summary: Headings and labels describe topic or purpose.

rows.title: Focus visible
rows.summary: Any keyboard operable interface has a visible focus indicator.

rows.title: Pointer gestures
rows.summary: Functionality that uses multipoint or path-based gestures has alternatives.

rows.title: Pointer cancellation
rows.summary: Functions triggered by single pointer can be cancelled or undone.

rows.title: Label in name
rows.summary: The accessible name contains the visible label text.

rows.title: Motion actuation
rows.summary: Functionality triggered by device motion can be disabled and has alternatives.

rows.title: Language of page
rows.summary: The default human language of each page can be programmatically determined.

rows.title: Language of parts
rows.summary: The human language of each passage can be programmatically determined.

rows.title: On focus
rows.summary: When a component receives focus, it does not initiate a change of context.

rows.title: On input
rows.summary: Changing settings of a component does not automatically cause context changes.

rows.title: Consistent navigation
rows.summary: Navigational mechanisms are repeated in the same relative order.

rows.title: Consistent identification
rows.summary: Components with the same functionality are identified consistently.

rows.title: Error identification
rows.summary: Input errors are automatically detected and described to the user.

rows.title: Labels or instructions
rows.summary: Labels or instructions are provided when content requires user input.

rows.title: Error suggestion
rows.summary: Input error suggestions are provided when errors are detected.

rows.title: Error prevention (legal, financial, data)
rows.summary: Important transactions can be reversed, checked, or confirmed.

rows.title: Parsing
rows.summary: Markup can be reliably interpreted: elements have complete tags, are nested correctly, and do not contain duplicate attributes or non-unique IDs. Obsolete in WCAG 2.2 but still part of WCAG 2.1 and EN 301 549 v3.2.1.

rows.title: Name, role, value
rows.summary: Name, role, and value can be programmatically determined for UI components.

rows.title: Status messages
rows.summary: Status messages can be programmatically determined through role or properties.

rows.title: WCAG conformance requirements
rows.summary: Web pages must satisfy all five WCAG 2.1 conformance requirements at Level AA: conformance level, full pages, complete processes, accessibility-supported ways of using technologies, and non-interference.

rows.title: Audio-only and video-only (pre-recorded - open functionality)
rows.summary: Provide alternatives for prerecorded audio-only and video-only content.

rows.title: Pre-recorded audio-only (closed functionality)
rows.summary: Where software is closed to screen readers and pre-recorded audio is needed to use closed functions, it must meet clause 5.1.5 by providing equivalent visual information.

rows.title: Pre-recorded video-only (closed functionality)
rows.summary: Where software is closed to assistive technology and pre-recorded video is needed to use closed functions, it must meet clause 5.1.3.7 by speaking equivalent information for the video content.

rows.title: Captions (pre-recorded)
rows.summary: Captions are provided for all prerecorded audio content in synchronized media.

rows.title: Audio description or media alternative (pre-recorded - open functionality)
rows.summary: Audio description or full text alternative is provided for prerecorded video content.

rows.title: Audio description or media alternative (pre-recorded - closed functionality)
rows.summary: Where software is closed to screen readers, it must meet clause 5.1.3.7: speech output presents equivalent information for pre-recorded video.

rows.title: Captions (live)
rows.summary: Captions are provided for all live audio content in synchronized media.

rows.title: Audio description (pre-recorded)
rows.summary: Audio description is provided for all prerecorded video content.

rows.title: Info and relationships (open functionality)
rows.summary: Information, structure, and relationships can be programmatically determined.

rows.title: Info and relationships (closed functionality)
rows.summary: Advisory: where software is closed to screen readers and information is on screen, auditory output should let the user correlate the audio with the display.

rows.title: Meaningful sequence (open functionality)
rows.summary: Content can be presented in a meaningful sequence without losing meaning.

rows.title: Meaningful sequence (closed functionality)
rows.summary: Advisory: where software is closed to screen readers and information is on screen, auditory output should follow a sequence the user can correlate with the display.

rows.title: Sensory characteristics
rows.summary: Instructions don't rely solely on sensory characteristics of components.

rows.title: Orientation
rows.summary: Content does not restrict its view to a single display orientation.

rows.title: Identify input purpose (open functionality)
rows.summary: The purpose of input fields can be programmatically determined.

rows.title: Identify input purpose (closed functionality)
rows.summary: Where software is closed to assistive technology, at least one mode must present the purpose of each personal-data input field in audio form.

rows.title: Use of colour
rows.summary: Color is not used as the only visual means of conveying information.

rows.title: Audio control
rows.summary: Audio that plays automatically can be paused, stopped, or controlled.

rows.title: Contrast (minimum)
rows.summary: Text has a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 (3:1 for large text).

rows.title: Resize text (open functionality)
rows.summary: Text can be resized up to 200% without loss of content or functionality.

rows.title: Resize text (closed functionality)
rows.summary: Where software cannot access platform text-enlargement features, it must meet clause 5.1.4 by providing its own legible text mode.

rows.title: Images of text (open functionality)
rows.summary: Text is used instead of images of text, except for customizable or essential images.

rows.title: Images of text (closed functionality)
rows.summary: Where software is closed to screen readers, it must meet clause 5.1.3.6: text rendered as images is still delivered via speech output.

rows.title: Void
rows.summary: Void. This slot keeps WCAG numbering alignment; the corresponding WCAG 2.1 criterion is Level AAA and is not required by EN 301 549.

rows.title: Void
rows.summary: Void. This slot keeps WCAG numbering alignment; the corresponding WCAG 2.1 criterion is Level AAA and is not required by EN 301 549.

rows.title: Void
rows.summary: Void. This slot keeps WCAG numbering alignment; the corresponding WCAG 2.1 criterion is Level AAA and is not required by EN 301 549.

rows.title: Void
rows.summary: Void. This slot keeps WCAG numbering alignment; the corresponding WCAG 2.1 criterion is Level AAA and is not required by EN 301 549.

rows.title: Reflow
rows.summary: Content can be presented without horizontal scrolling at 320 CSS pixels width.

rows.title: Non-text contrast
rows.summary: UI components and graphical objects have sufficient contrast (3:1 minimum).

rows.title: Text spacing
rows.summary: No loss of content when text spacing is adjusted within certain parameters.

rows.title: Content on hover or focus
rows.summary: Additional content triggered by hover or focus can be dismissed and doesn't interfere.

rows.title: Keyboard (open functionality)
rows.summary: All functionality is available from a keyboard interface.

rows.title: Keyboard (closed functionality)
rows.summary: Where software is closed to keyboards and keyboard interfaces, it must meet clause 5.1.6.1: all functionality operable without vision.

rows.title: No keyboard trap
rows.summary: Focus can be moved away from any component using standard keyboard methods.

rows.title: Void
rows.summary: Void. This slot keeps WCAG numbering alignment; the corresponding WCAG 2.1 criterion is Level AAA and is not required by EN 301 549.

rows.title: Character key shortcuts (open functionality)
rows.summary: Single character key shortcuts can be turned off or remapped.

rows.title: Character key shortcuts (closed functionality)
rows.summary: Where software is closed to keyboards and keyboard interfaces, it must meet clause 5.1.6.1 rather than the character-key-shortcuts criterion.

rows.title: Timing adjustable
rows.summary: Users can turn off, adjust, or extend time limits.

rows.title: Pause, stop, hide
rows.summary: Moving, blinking, or auto-updating content can be paused, stopped, or hidden.

rows.title: Three flashes or below threshold
rows.summary: Content does not contain anything that flashes more than three times per second.

rows.title: Void
rows.summary: Void. The corresponding WCAG criterion is not applied in this context by EN 301 549 v3.2.1.

rows.title: Void
rows.summary: Void. The corresponding WCAG criterion is not applied in this context by EN 301 549 v3.2.1.

rows.title: Focus order
rows.summary: Focusable components receive focus in an order that preserves meaning.

rows.title: Link purpose (in context)
rows.summary: The purpose of each link can be determined from link text or context.

rows.title: Void
rows.summary: Void. The corresponding WCAG criterion is not applied in this context by EN 301 549 v3.2.1.

rows.title: Headings and labels
rows.summary: Headings and labels describe topic or purpose.

rows.title: Focus visible
rows.summary: Any keyboard operable interface has a visible focus indicator.

rows.title: Pointer gestures
rows.summary: Functionality that uses multipoint or path-based gestures has alternatives.

rows.title: Pointer cancellation
rows.summary: Functions triggered by single pointer can be cancelled or undone.

rows.title: Label in name (open functionality)
rows.summary: The accessible name contains the visible label text.

rows.title: Label in name (closed functionality)
rows.summary: Advisory: where software is closed to screen readers, it should meet clause 5.1.3.3 on auditory output correlation.

rows.title: Motion actuation
rows.summary: Functionality triggered by device motion can be disabled and has alternatives.

rows.title: Language of software (open functionality)
rows.summary: The default human language of each page can be programmatically determined.

rows.title: Language of software (closed functionality)
rows.summary: Where software is closed to screen readers, it must meet clause 5.1.3.14: speech output in the same human language as the displayed content.

rows.title: Void
rows.summary: Void. The corresponding WCAG criterion is not applied in this context by EN 301 549 v3.2.1.

rows.title: On focus
rows.summary: When a component receives focus, it does not initiate a change of context.

rows.title: On input
rows.summary: Changing settings of a component does not automatically cause context changes.

rows.title: Void
rows.summary: Void. The corresponding WCAG criterion is not applied in this context by EN 301 549 v3.2.1.

rows.title: Void
rows.summary: Void. The corresponding WCAG criterion is not applied in this context by EN 301 549 v3.2.1.

rows.title: Error identification (open functionality)
rows.summary: Input errors are automatically detected and described to the user.

rows.title: Error Identification (closed functionality)
rows.summary: Where software is closed to screen readers, it must meet clause 5.1.3.15: speech output identifies and describes detected input errors.

rows.title: Labels or instructions
rows.summary: Labels or instructions are provided when content requires user input.

rows.title: Error suggestion
rows.summary: Input error suggestions are provided when errors are detected.

rows.title: Error prevention (legal, financial, data)
rows.summary: Important transactions can be reversed, checked, or confirmed.

rows.title: Parsing (open functionality)
rows.summary: Markup can be reliably interpreted: elements have complete tags, are nested correctly, and do not contain duplicate attributes or non-unique IDs. Obsolete in WCAG 2.2 but still part of WCAG 2.1 and EN 301 549 v3.2.1.

rows.title: Parsing (closed functionality)
rows.summary: Not applicable. Software closed to all assistive technology does not have to meet the Parsing criterion, whose intent is exposing information to assistive technology.

rows.title: Name, role, value (open functionality)
rows.summary: Name, role, and value can be programmatically determined for UI components.

rows.title: Name, role, value (closed functionality)
rows.summary: Not applicable. Software closed to all assistive technology does not have to meet Name, Role, Value, which exists to serve assistive technology interoperability.

rows.title: Status messages (open functionality)
rows.summary: Status messages can be programmatically determined through role or properties.

rows.title: Status messages (closed functionality)
rows.summary: Not applicable. Software closed to all assistive technology does not have to meet Status Messages, which exists to serve assistive technology interoperability.

rows.title: Closed functionality
rows.summary: Software whose closed functionality conforms to clause 5.1 does not additionally need to meet the assistive-technology interoperability requirements of 11.5.2.

rows.title: Platform accessibility service support for software that provides a user interface
rows.summary: Platform software must provide documented services that let software with a user interface interoperate with assistive technology.

rows.title: Platform accessibility service support for assistive technologies
rows.summary: Platform software must provide documented accessibility services that let assistive technology interoperate with software running on the platform.

rows.title: Use of accessibility services
rows.summary: Software with a user interface must use the platform's documented accessibility services; where those are insufficient, other documented services may be used.

rows.title: Assistive technology
rows.summary: Assistive technology itself must use the documented platform accessibility services.

rows.title: Object information
rows.summary: The role, states, boundary, name, and description of every user interface element must be programmatically determinable by assistive technology.

rows.title: Row, column, and headers
rows.summary: The row, column, and any headers of each data table cell must be programmatically determinable by assistive technology.

rows.title: Values
rows.summary: Current, minimum, and maximum values of a ranged element (such as a slider) must be programmatically determinable by assistive technology.

rows.title: Label relationships
rows.summary: Label relationships between elements (labels and labelled-by) must be exposed to assistive technology.

rows.title: Parent-child relationships
rows.summary: Parent-child relationships between elements must be programmatically determinable by assistive technology.

rows.title: Text
rows.summary: Text contents, text attributes, and the boundary of text on screen must be programmatically determinable by assistive technology.

rows.title: List of available actions
rows.summary: A list of the actions available on an element must be programmatically determinable by assistive technology.

rows.title: Execution of available actions
rows.summary: Where security permits, assistive technology must be able to programmatically execute those exposed actions.

rows.title: Tracking of focus and selection attributes
rows.summary: Information needed to track focus, the text insertion point, and selection attributes must be exposed to assistive technology.

rows.title: Modification of focus and selection attributes
rows.summary: Where security permits, assistive technology must be able to programmatically move focus, the text insertion point, and selection.

rows.title: Change notification
rows.summary: Assistive technology must be notified of changes to the programmatically determinable attributes of elements.

rows.title: Modifications of states and properties
rows.summary: Where security permits, assistive technology must be able to modify states and properties of elements, where the user can modify them.

rows.title: Modifications of values and text
rows.summary: Where security permits, assistive technology must be able to modify values and text of elements, where the user can modify them.

rows.title: User control of accessibility features
rows.summary: Platform software must give users control over the platform accessibility features documented as intended for users.

rows.title: No disruption of accessibility features
rows.summary: Software must not disrupt documented platform accessibility features, except when the user asks it to.

rows.title: User preferences
rows.summary: Software that is not isolated from its platform must follow the user's platform preferences for measurement units, colour, contrast, font type, font size, and focus cursor, unless overridden by the user.

rows.title: Content technology
rows.summary: Authoring tools must meet clauses 11.8.2 to 11.8.5 to the extent that the output format supports the relevant accessibility information.

rows.title: Accessible content creation
rows.summary: Authoring tools must enable and guide the production of content that conforms to clause 9 (web) or 10 (documents) as applicable.

rows.title: Preservation of accessibility information in transformations
rows.summary: Restructuring and re-coding transformations must preserve accessibility information where the output technology can hold it.

rows.title: Repair assistance
rows.summary: Where an authoring tool's checker detects a failure against clause 9 or 10, it must offer repair suggestions.

rows.title: Templates
rows.summary: Where templates are offered, at least one accessible template supporting conformant content must be available and identified as such.

rows.title: Accessibility and compatibility features
rows.summary: Product documentation must list and explain how to use the ICT's accessibility and compatibility features.

rows.title: Accessible documentation
rows.summary: Product documentation must be available in an accessible electronic format: web content conforming to clause 9, or a non-web document conforming to clause 10.

rows.title: Information on accessibility and compatibility features
rows.summary: Support services must be able to give information about the accessibility and compatibility features mentioned in the documentation.

rows.title: Effective communication
rows.summary: Support services must accommodate the communication needs of people with disabilities, directly or through a referral point.

rows.title: Accessible documentation
rows.summary: Documentation provided by support services must be available in an accessible electronic format conforming to clause 9 or clause 10.

rows.title: Text relay services
rows.summary: A text relay service must let text users and speech users interact by converting between the two modes of communication.

rows.title: Sign relay services
rows.summary: A sign relay service must let sign language users and speech users interact through interpretation.

rows.title: Lip-reading relay services
rows.summary: A lip-reading relay service must let lip-readers and voice telephone users interact.

rows.title: Captioned telephony services
rows.summary: A captioned telephony service must caption the incoming side of a conversation for a deaf or hard of hearing user.

rows.title: Speech to speech relay services
rows.summary: A speech-to-speech relay service must enable telephone use by people with speech impairments or limited cognition, language, or learning.

rows.title: Access to relay services
rows.summary: Where a system is specified for use with relay services, access to those relay services must not be blocked for outgoing or incoming voice, RTT, or video calls.

rows.title: Access to emergency services
rows.summary: Where a system is specified for use with emergency services, access to those emergency services must not be blocked for outgoing or incoming voice, RTT, or video calls.
